This is because problem-solving, innovation and critical thinking skills cannot be outsourced or easily acquired by competitors. This unit is designed to develop your understanding of how businesses operate. It shows how information systems support business operations and management through integration of people, business processes and systems. You will be provided with an introduction to state-of-the-art business analysis techniques, frameworks and models to assist in understanding the nature and contribution of BIS in a range of business contexts. With its emphasis on business rather than IT, this unit does not require prior IT-related experience. In this unit, you will learn about the increasingly important role of IT in business and acquire valuable business analysis and problem-solving skills.

text: This unit introduces students to the foundations of project management in business contexts. It provides an overview and practical understanding of different project management approaches, ranging from structured frameworks such as the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) to light-weight techniques such as Agile or Lean Management. Students learn how to select appropriate projects based on their alignment with an organisation's strategy and then how to manage those projects successfully from initiation through execution to completion. The unit explores both the technical and behavioural aspects of project management and students gain experience in critically analysing the application of techniques in specific business contexts. As organisations increasingly structure their activities on a project basis, the unit is of value to a range of discipline specialisations.

label: Overview paragraph 1
text: Despite the widely acknowledged importance of data as a strategic resource, organisations continue to struggle with appropriately managing their data assets. This unit highlights the crucial importance of data governance in the administration, protection, and optimisation of data. It provides an exploration into the core principles of data governance, discusses the influence of emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, and examines the broader societal and ethical implications surrounding data. Through interactive case studies and hands-on assessments, students learn about the complex issues surrounding data governance and formulate and persuasively communicate practical data governance approaches to empower organisations to navigate their data landscape.
